name: Ion-Channel Receptor
description:
# Ion Channel Receptor
Ions
Ligand (such as acetylcholine)
This is an example of an ion channel-receptor. On the left, the channel is closed, because the ligand (dark purple triangle) has not binded to the receptor. When the ligand binds to the receptor, the channel opens, and the ions (orange circles) can freely flow through the membrane.

In a neuromuscular junction, these are used to transfer the action potential from the neuron to the muscle. The ligand is acetylcholine, and when it binds to the ion channel receptor on the membrane of the muscle, the channel opens and allows sodium ions to flow into the muscle.
creator: Isaac Webb

name: Membrane Permeability of a Neuron During an Action Potential
description:
Key:(a)  Sodium (Na+) ion(b)  Potassium (K+) ion(c)  Sodium channel(d)  Potassium channel(e)  Sodium-Potassium Pump
In the stages of an action potential, the permeability of the membrane of the neuron changes. At the resting state (1), sodium and potassium ions are unable to pass through the membrane, and the neuron has a negative charge inside (mainly due to the large proteins that are negatively charged, as well as the lower amount of positive K+ ions inside the neuron). Once the action potential is triggered, the depolarization (2) of the neuron activates the sodium channel, allowing sodium ions to pass through the membrane of the neuron and results in a positive charge in the neuron and a negative charge in the extracellular fluid. After the action potential is reached, the neuron begins repolarization (3), where the sodium channels close and the potassium channels open, allowing potassium ions to cross the membrane and flood into the extracellular fluid, resulting in a positive charge in the extracellular fluid and a negative charge that is below the resting potential of the neuron. Finally, the membrane potential returns to the resting state as the potassium channels close during the refractory period (4). The sodium-potassium pump works to maintain the concentration gradient over time by exchanging three sodium ions per two potassium ions across the plasma membrane .https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UabDiuTtU0Mhttps://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UabDiuTtU0M

name: Propagation of action potential along myelinated nerve fiber en
description:
Translation and vector of the File:Propagation of action potential along myelinated nerve fiber.png Image description: Schematic representation of the action potential propagation through myelinated nerve fiber of peripheral nervous system. From axon hillock of neuron body (soma) action potential propagates from one unmyelinated fiber part to the next one. The unmyelinated parts of the nerve fiber are 
nodes of Ranvier. This way of action potential propagation is called saltatory conduction (red arrows in the diagram) Ion channels open, allow sodium ions to enter the cell leading to membrane depolarization and generation of action potential.  Myelination of nerve fibers in the peripheral nervous system is achieved by Schwann cells wrapping around an axon part (cross section). The nucleus and most of the Schwan cell cytoplasm are contained in the outer most layer called neurilemma.  Own work loosely based on Raphael Alya R., Talbot William S. (2011). name: Phage Therapy
description: Phage therapy is the use of bacteriophages to treat bacterial infections. This could be used as an alternative to antibiotics when bacteria develops resistance. Superbugs that are immune to multiple types of drugs are becoming a concern with the more frequent use of antibiotics. Phages can target these dangerous microbes without harming human cells due to how specific they are. When bacteria develop immunity to phages they generally have to give up their antibiotic resistance, always leaving a weakness that allows us to treat against them.

name: Estructura y genoma del coronavirus SARS-CoV-2
description: SARSCoV2 pertenece a la familia Coronaviridae, genero beta-coronavirus grupo 2b. Son virus del grupo IV de la clasificación de Baltimore. Es un virus con envoltura de un tamaño aproximado entre 100-160 nanómetros. La envoltura presenta unas espículas que se proyectan hacia el exterior formadas por trímeros de la glicoproteína S. En la envoltura también se localizan las proteínas E y M, esencial para el ensamblaje del virus. En el interior se localiza la nucleocápside helicoidal formada por el genoma del virus rodeado por la proteína N. El genoma consiste en una molécula de ARN mono cadena sentido positivo de unos 30 Kb. Su estructura es muy similar a la de una ARN mensajero, con su capuchón en el extremo 5´y su cola de poly adeninas en el extremo 3´. Los genes que codifican para las proteínas reguladores se sitúan en el extremo 5´y los que codifican para las proteínas estructurales (S, E, M, N) en el 3´. Los genes reguladores se organizan en dos marcos de lectura (ORF1 y ORF2), que darán lugar, entre otras proteínas, a las proteasa PLpro y 3CLpro, a la enzima ARN polimerasa dependiente de ARN  (RdRp) y a la helicasa (Hel). Referencia: SARS and MERS: recent insights into emerging coronaviruses. de Wit E, van Doremalen N, Falzarano D, Munster VJ. Nat Rev Microbiol. 2016 Aug;14(8):523-34. doi: 10.1038/nrmicro.2016.81. https://www.nature.com/articles/nrmicro.2016.81#MOESM6

name: Domestic dog
description: Domestic dog - The dog (Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris) is a domesticated descendant of the gray wolf. Also known as the domestic dog, it was selectively bred from an extinct wolf population during the Late Pleistocene by hunter-gatherers. Dogs were the first species to be domesticated by humans, over 14,000 years ago, even before agriculture emerged. Thanks to their long relationship with humans, dogs have developed the ability to thrive on a starch-rich diet, which would not be suitable for other canid species.

name: Domestic Cat
description: Domestic Cat - The domestic cat (Felis catus), also known as the house cat, is a small carnivorous mammal that has been domesticated. It is the only species within the Felidae family that has been domesticated. Through studies in archaeology and genetics, it has been determined that cats were domesticated in the Near East around 7500 BC. Cats are commonly kept as pets or farm animals but also live independently as feral creatures, often avoiding human interaction. Valued by people for their companionship and their ability to control pests, they are skilled at hunting vermin. With retractable claws designed for capturing small prey like mice and rats, they possess a strong, agile body, quick reflexes, and sharp teeth. Cats are known for their excellent night vision and keen sense of smell. While they are social animals, they hunt alone and are most active during dawn and dusk.

name: HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)
description: HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) - The human immunodeficiency viruses (HIV) are two types of Lentivirus—a subgroup of retroviruses—that infect humans. Over time, HIV leads to acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), a condition marked by the gradual breakdown of the immune system, making the body vulnerable to life-threatening opportunistic infections and cancers. Without treatment, the average life expectancy after contracting HIV is estimated to be between 9 and 11 years, depending on the specific subtype.

description: Blood Smear Unstained - A blood smear—also known as a peripheral blood smear or blood film—is a thin layer of blood spread onto a glass microscope slide and stained to enable microscopic examination of the different blood cells. Blood smears are used in the evaluation of hematological disorders and are routinely performed to detect blood parasites, including those that cause malaria and filariasis.
creator: NIH NIAID BioArt (Ryan Kissinger)

name: Blood Smear Wright-Giemsa Stain
description: Blood Smear Wright-Giemsa Stain - A blood smear—also known as a peripheral blood smear or blood film—is a thin layer of blood spread onto a glass microscope slide and stained to enable microscopic examination of the different blood cells. Blood smears are used in the evaluation of hematological disorders and are routinely performed to detect blood parasites, including those that cause malaria and filariasis. Wright’s stain is a hematologic stain used to distinguish different types of blood cells. It traditionally consists of a mixture of eosin (red) and methylene blue dyes. The stain is primarily applied to peripheral blood smears, urine samples, and bone marrow aspirates for examination under a light microscope. In cytogenetics, Wright’s stain is also used to stain chromosomes, aiding in the diagnosis of various syndromes and diseases.

name: Hantavirus
description: Hantavirus - Orthohantaviruses are a genus of viruses that includes all hantaviruses known to cause disease in humans. These viruses are primarily maintained in rodent populations, with each hantavirus species typically associated with a specific rodent host. In their natural rodent reservoirs, hantaviruses usually establish persistent infections without causing symptoms. In humans, however, hantavirus infection can result in two serious illnesses: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS). HFRS is predominantly associated with Old World hantaviruses found in Africa, Asia, and Europe, whereas HPS is primarily caused by New World hantaviruses circulating in the Americas.
creator: NIH NIAID BioArt (Ryan Kissinger)

name: Toxoplasma gondii Tachyzoite
description: Toxoplasma gondii Tachyzoite - Toxoplasma gondii is a globally distributed parasitic protozoan that causes toxoplasmosis. It can infect nearly all warm-blooded animals, including humans, birds, and other mammals. However, members of the cat family (Felidae) are the only known definitive hosts in which the parasite completes its sexual reproductive cycle. As a result, cats play a central role in the transmission and life cycle of T. gondii.

name: ANGIOTENSINOGEN

name: Antigen presenting cell
description: An antigen-presenting cell, or accessory cell, is a cell that displays antigen complexed with major histocompatibility complexes (MHCs) on their surfaces; this process is known as antigen presentation. T cells may recognize these complexes using their T cell receptors (TCRs). These cells process antigens and present them to T-cells
creator: Steve Jupe

name: Antimicrobial peptides
description: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), also called host defense peptides (HDPs) are part of the innate immune response found among all classes of life

name: Antiporter 01
description: An antiporter is a cotransporter and integral membrane protein involved in secondary active transport of two or more different molecules or ions across a phospholipid membrane such as the plasma membrane in opposite directions

name: APC/C complex
description: Also known as Anaphase-promoting complex is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that marks target cell cycle proteins for degradation by the 26S proteasome

name: AUG start codon

description: A protein complex that is located in the cytosol and contains one or more cysteine-type endopeptidases (also called caspases), which give the complex a peptidase activity with specificity for the hydrolysis of aspartyl bonds. These complexes may be involved e.g. in apoptotic or inflammation processes
creator: Veronica Shamovsky

name: Caveolin
description: Caveolins are a family of integral membrane proteins that are the principal components of caveolae membranes and involved in receptor-independent endocytosis

name: CCA ending

name: Centriole
description: A centriole is a cylindrical cell structure composed mainly of a protein called tubulin that is found in most eukaryotic cells

name: Centromere
description: The centromere is the specialized DNA sequence of a chromosome that links a pair of sister chromatids. During mitosis, spindle fibers attach to the centromere via the kinetochore. Centromeres were first thought to be genetic loci that direct the behavior of chromosomes

name: Chylomicron

Their cytoplasmic surface is coated with a bristlelike structure made of clathrin. During the first steps of endocytosis, clathrin-coated pits are internalized to form clathrin-coated vesicles which transport proteins from organelle to organelle

name: CLOCK

name: CORTICOTROPIN
description: A polypeptide hormone produced and secreted by the pituitary gland comprising 39 amino acid residues coupled in a linear sequence. The N-terminal 24-amino acid segment is identical in all species and contains the adrenocorticotrophic activity. Corticotropin stimulates the cortex of the adrenal gland and boosts the synthesis of corticosteroids, mainly glucocorticoids but also sex steroids (androgens). It is used in the treatment of certain neurological disorders such as infantile spasms and multiple sclerosis, and diagnostically to investigate adrenocortical insufficiency
creator: Bruce May

name: CORTISOL
description: Cortisol is a steroid hormone, in the glucocorticoid class of hormones

name: GPCR CLASS B 2

name: GPCR generic

name: gRNA

name: Growth hormone receptor

name: Gulose

name: HDL

creator: Steve Jupe

name: Hemoglobin
description: Hemoglobin, or haemoglobin, is the iron-containing oxygen-transport metalloprotein in the red blood cells of all vertebrates
creator: Steve Jupe

As a medication, it is used to decrease pressure in the eyes, as in glaucoma, and to lower increased intracranial pressure

creator: Bruce May

name: Ena/VASP Proteins
description: ENA/VASP Homology proteins or EVH proteins are a family of closely related proteins involved in cell motility in vertebrate and invertebrate animals
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: MT-CO3
description: Mitochondrially encoded cytochrome c oxidase III
creator: Bruce May

name: ABL
description: Generic representation of Tyrosine-protein kinase ABL1 or ABL2
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: CASTOR1
description: Cytosolic arginine sensor for mTORC1 subunit 1
creator: Bruce May

name: TIFA
description: TRAF-interacting protein with FHA domain-containing protein A
creator: Veronica Shamovsky

name: mTORC1
description: mTORC1, also known as mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 or mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1, is a protein complex that functions as a nutrient/energy/redox sensor and controls protein synthesis. mTOR Complex 1 (mTORC1) is composed of mTOR itself, regulatory-associated protein of mTOR (Raptor), mammalian lethal with SEC13 protein 8 (MLST8), PRAS40 and DEPTOR. This complex embodies the classic functions of mTOR, namely as a nutrient/energy/redox sensor and controller of protein synthesis. The activity of this complex is regulated by rapamycin, insulin, growth factors, phosphatidic acid, certain amino acids and their derivatives (e.g., l-leucine and β-hydroxy β-methylbutyric acid), mechanical stimuli, and oxidative stress
creator: Bruce May

name: Myristoyl group
description: A straight-chain, fourteen-carbon, long-chain saturated fatty acid mostly found in milk fat
creator: Bruce May

name: RRAGA,B
description: Ras-related GTP-binding protein A and B
creator: Bruce May

name: Ragulator
description: Ragulator complex protein LAMTOR1, LAMTOR2, LAMTOR3, LAMTOR4 and LAMTOR5
creator: Bruce May

name: RRAGC,D
description: Ras-related GTP-binding protein C and D
creator: Bruce May

name: DHA
description: A docosahexaenoic acid having six cis-double bonds at positions 4, 7, 10, 13, 16 and 19
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Selenium
description: Selenium is a chemical element with the symbol Se and atomic number 34. It is a nonmetal (more rarely considered a metalloid) with properties that are intermediate between the elements above and below in the periodic table, sulfur and tellurium, and also has similarities to arsenic. It rarely occurs in its elemental state or as pure ore compounds in the Earth's crust. Selenium – from Ancient Greek σελήνη (selḗnē) "Moon" – was discovered in 1817 by Jöns Jacob Berzelius, who noted the similarity of the new element to the previously discovered tellurium (named for the Earth)
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Fumarate
description: A hydrogen butenedioate obtained by deprotonation of one of the carboxy groups of fumaric acid
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Tyrosine
description: An amino acid zwitterion arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-tyrosine; major species at pH 7.3
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Urea
description: A carbonyl group with two C-bound amine groups
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Glycine
description: An amino acid zwitterion arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of glycine
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Tryptophan
description: L-tryptophan zwitterion. An L-α-amino acid zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-tryptophan; major species at pH 7.3
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Oxaloacetate
description: Also known as oxaloacetic acid, an oxodicarboxylic acid that is succinic acid bearing a single oxo group
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Lysine
description: A diamino acid that is caproic (hexanoic) acid bearing two amino substituents at positions 2 and 6
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Protectins
description: The protectin (PD) family of specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) is biosynthesised from docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and n–3 docosapentaenoic acid (n–3 DPA). All of the PDs show anti-inflammatory and pro-resolving actions
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Succinyl-CoA
description: An ω-carboxyacyl-CoA having succinoyl as the S-acyl component
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Phospholipids
description: Phospholipids are a class of lipids that are a major component of all cell membranes. They can form lipid bilayers because of their amphiphilic characteristic. The structure of the phospholipid molecule generally consists of two hydrophobic fatty acid "tails" and a hydrophilic "head" consisting of a phosphate group. The two components are usually joined together by a glycerol molecule. The phosphate groups can be modified with simple organic molecules such as choline, ethanolamine or serine
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Creatinine
description: A lactam obtained by formal cyclocondensation of creatine. It is a metabolite of creatine
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Selenoproteins
description: In molecular biology a selenoprotein is any protein that includes a selenocysteine (Sec, U, Se-Cys) amino acid residue. Among functionally characterized selenoproteins are five glutathione peroxidases (GPX) and three thioredoxin reductases, (TrxR/TXNRD) which both contain only one Sec. Selenoprotein P is the most common selenoprotein found in the plasma. It is unusual because in humans it contains 10 Sec residues, which are split into two domains, a longer N-terminal domain that contains 1 Sec, and a shorter C-terminal domain that contains 9 Sec. The longer N-terminal domain is likely an enzymatic domain, and the shorter C-terminal domain is likely a means of safely transporting the very reactive selenium atom throughout the body
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: EPA
description: An icosapentaenoic acid having five cis-double bonds at positions 5, 8, 11, 14 and 17
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Resolvins
description: Resolvins are metabolic byproducts of omega-3 fatty acids, primarily eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), as well as docosapentaenoic acid (DPA) and clupanodonic acid. As autacoids similar to hormones acting on local tissues, resolvins are under preliminary research for their involvement in promoting restoration of normal cellular function following the inflammation that occurs after tissue injury. Resolvins belong to a class of polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) metabolites termed specialized proresolving mediators (SPMs)
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Maresins
description: Maresin 1 (MaR1 or 7R,14S-dihydroxy-4Z,8E,10E,12Z,16Z,19Z-docosahexaenoic acid) is a macrophage-derived mediator of inflammation resolution coined from macrophage mediator in resolving inflammation. Maresin 1, and more recently defined maresins, are 12-lipoxygenase-derived metabolites of the omega-3 fatty acid, docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), that possess potent anti-inflammatory, pro-resolving, protective, and pro-healing properties similar to a variety of other members of the specialized proresolving mediators (SPM) class of polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) metabolites
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Electrophilic omega 3 oxo-derivatives
description: Electrophilic oxo-derivatives of ω-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (ω-3 PUFAs) are generated in macrophages and neutrophils in response to inflammation and oxidative stress to promote the resolution of inflammation. Being electrophilic, these derivatives reversibly bind to nucleophilic residues on target proteins, triggering the activation of cytoprotective pathways. These electrophilic derivatives transduce anti-inflammatory actions rather than suppress the production of pro-inflammatory arachidonic acid metabolites
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Electron Transport Chain
description: The electron transport chain (Figure 1) is the last component of aerobic respiration and is the only part of glucose metabolism that uses atmospheric oxygen
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: FADH2
description: FAD can be reduced to FADH2 through the addition of 2 H+ and 2 e−. FADH2 can also be oxidized by the loss of 1 H+ and 1 e− to form FADH
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: AMPK
description: Generic representation for AMP-activated protein kinase
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Acylcarnitine
description: Any carboxylic ester obtained by the O-acylation of carnitine
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Lipoxins
description: Lipoxins (LXs or Lxs), an acronym for lipoxygenase interaction products, are bioactive autacoid metabolites of arachidonic acid made by various cell types. They are categorized as nonclassic eicosanoids and members of the specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) family of polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) metabolites. Like other SPMs, LXs form during, and then act to resolve, inflammatory responses
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Linoleic Acid
description: An octadecadienoic acid in which the two double bonds are at positions 9 and 12 and have Z (cis) stereochemistry
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Docosapentaenoic acid
description: Any straight-chain, C22 fatty acid having five C=C double bonds
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Carnitine
description: An amino-acid betaine that is butanoate substituted with a hydroxy group at position C-3 and a trimethylammonium group at C-4
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: alpha-Linolenoyl-CoA
description: An octadecatrienoyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of α-linolenic acid
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Citrate
description: A tricarboxylic acid that is propane-1,2,3-tricarboxylic acid bearing a hydroxy substituent at position 2. It is an important metabolite in the pathway of all aerobic organisms
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Polyunsaturated fatty acid
description: Any fatty acid containing more than one double bond. Acids in this group are reported to have cardioprotective effects; and levels are lowered in chronic fatigue syndrome
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Arachidonic Acid
description: A long-chain fatty acid that is a C20, polyunsaturated fatty acid having four (Z)-double bonds at positions 5, 8, 11 and 14
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Inositol Phosphates
description: Inositol phosphates are a group of mono- to polyphosphorylated inositols. They play crucial roles in diverse cellular functions, such as cell growth, apoptosis, cell migration, endocytosis, and cell differentiation
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: L-Aspartate
description: An aspartate(1−) that is the conjugate base of L-aspartic acid
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Carbovir Triphosphate
description: The organic triphosphate that is the 5'-triphosphate of (−)-carbovir
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Cofactors
description: An organic molecule or ion (usually a metal ion) that is required by an enzyme for its activity. It may be attached either loosely (coenzyme) or tightly (prosthetic group)
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Steroids
description: Any of naturally occurring compounds and synthetic analogues, based on the cyclopenta[a]phenanthrene carbon skeleton, partially or completely hydrogenated; there are usually methyl groups at C-10 and C-13, and often an alkyl group at C-17. By extension, one or more bond scissions, ring expansions and/or ring contractions of the skeleton may have occurred. Natural steroids are derived biogenetically from squalene, so may be considered as triterpenoids
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Porphyrins
description: Porphyrins ( POR-fər-in) are a group of heterocyclic macrocycle organic compounds, composed of four modified pyrrole subunits interconnected at their α carbon atoms via methine bridges (=CH−). The parent porphyrin is porphine, a rare chemical compound of exclusively theoretical interest. Substituted porphines are called porphyrins
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Active Vitamin Forms
description: Vitamins, which are generally obtained from dietary sources, are converted to their active forms to take part in biochemical processes
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: LACTATE
description: Lactic acid is an organic acid. It has a molecular formula CH3CH(OH)CO2H. It is white in solid state and it is miscible with water. While in liquid state (dissolved state) it is a colorless solution. Production includes both artificial synthesis as well as natural sources. Lactic acid is an alpha-hydroxy acid (AHA) due to the presence of carboxyl group adjacent to the hydroxyl group. It is used as a synthetic intermediate in many organic synthesis industries and in various biochemical industries
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Organism Proteins
description: Amino acid metabolism provides the precursors for an organism to synthezise and use proteins for a vast array of bodily functions and processes
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Linoleoyl-CoA
description: An octadecadienoyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of linoleic acid
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Cytokines
description: Cytokines are a broad and loose category of small proteins (~5–20 kDa) that are important in cell signaling. Cytokines are peptides, and cannot cross the lipid bilayer of cells to enter the cytoplasm. Cytokines have been shown to be involved in autocrine, paracrine and endocrine signaling as immunomodulating agents. Their definite distinction from hormones is still part of ongoing research. Cytokines include chemokines, interferons, interleukins, lymphokines, and tumour necrosis factors, but generally not hormones or growth factors (despite some overlap in the terminology). Cytokines are produced by a broad range of cells, including immune cells like macrophages, B lymphocytes, T lymphocytes and mast cells, as well as endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and various stromal cells; a given cytokine may be produced by more than one type of cell
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Specialised pro-resolving mediator
description: A class of cell signaling molecules enzymatically derived from n-3 long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids that have important roles in orchestrating the resolution of tissue inflammation
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: NADH
description: Dianion of NADH arising from deprotonation of the two diphosphate OH groups; major species at pH 7.3
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Membrane Phospholipids
description: Membrane phospholipids modulate signaling cascades, affecting the development, differentiation, function, and repair of the nervous system, functions that become dysregulated with ischemia and oxidative stress
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Sulfur
description: Sulfur is a chemical element with the symbol S and atomic number 16. It is abundant, multivalent, and nonmetallic. Under normal conditions, sulfur atoms form cyclic octatomic molecules with a chemical formula S8. Elemental sulfur is a bright yellow, crystalline solid at room temperature
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Eicosanoids
description: Eicosanoids are any member of the group of signalling molecules arising from oxidation of the three C20 essential fatty acids (EFAs) icosapentaenoic acid (EPA), arachidonic acid (AA) and dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid (DGLA)
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Xenobiotics
description: A xenobiotic (Greek, xenos "foreign"; bios "life") is a compound that is foreign to a living organism. Principal xenobiotics include: drugs, carcinogens and various compounds that have been introduced into the environment by artificial means
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Ketone bodies
description: A carbonyl compound produced as a water-soluble byproduct when fatty acids are broken down for energy in the liver. There are three endogenous ketone bodies: acetone, acetoacetic acid, and (R)-3-hydroxybutyric acid; others may be produced as a result of the metabolism of synthetic triglycerides
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Propionyl-CoA
description: An acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of propionic acid
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Alpha-linoleic acid
description: A linolenic acid with cis-double bonds at positions 9, 12 and 15. Shown to have an antithrombotic effect
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Malonyl-CoA
description: The S-malonyl derivative of coenzyme A
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: GCG
description: Glucagon plays a key role in glucose metabolism and homeostasis. Regulates blood glucose by increasing gluconeogenesis and decreasing glycolysis. A counterregulatory hormone of insulin, raises plasma glucose levels in response to insulin-induced hypoglycemia. Plays an important role in initiating and maintaining hyperglycemic conditions in diabetes
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Very Long-Chain fatty acyl-CoA
description: A fatty acyl-CoA in which the fatty acyl group has a chain length greater than C22
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: ABACAVIR
description: A 2,6-diaminopurine that is (1S)-cyclopent-2-en-1-ylmethanol in which the pro-R hydrogen at the 4-position is substituted by a 2-amino-6-(cyclopropylamino)-9H-purin-9-yl group. A nucleoside analogue reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) with antiretroviral activity against HIV, it is used (particularly as the sulfate) with other antiretrovirals in combination therapy of HIV infection
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Free Fatty Acids
description: Fatty acids circulating in plasma in their un-esterified form are called free fatty acids. In plasma, FFAs are always bound to a transport protein, usually albumin
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Bilirubin
description: A member of the class of biladienes that is a linear tetrapyrrole with the dipyrrole units being of both exovinyl and endovinyl type. A product of heme degradation, it is produced in the reticuloendothelial system by the reduction of biliverdin and transported to the liver as a complex with serum albumin
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Fatty Acyl-CoA
description: An acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of any fatty acid
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Phosphatidylglycerol
description: A glycerophosphoglycerol that is glycerol in which the hydrogen of one of the primary hydroxy groups has been replaced by a phosphatidyl group
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Steroid Hormones
description: Steroids that can act as hormones that mediate a wide range of physiological processes. The two main classes of steroid hormone are corticosteroids (glucocorticoids or mineralocorticoids) and sex hormones (adrogens, progestogens or estrogens)
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: CDP-ethanolamine
description: A phosphoethanolamine consisting of ethanolamine having a cytidine 5'-diphosphate moiety attached to the oxygen
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Sphingosine
description: A sphing-4-enine in which the double bond is trans
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Thiamine diphosphate
description: Dianion of thiamine(1+) diphosphate arising from deprotonation of the three OH groups of the diphosphate
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Lysophosphatidylserine
description: An acylglycerophosphoserine resulting from partial hydrolysis of a phosphatidylserine, which removes one of the fatty acid groups. The structure is depicted in the image where R1 = acyl, R2 = H or where R1 = H, R2 = acyl. Formula C7H13NO9PR, where R represents the hydrocarbon chain of the fatty acyl group
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: 1-acyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-D-myo-inositol
description: A 1-acylglycerophosphoinositol in which sn-glycerol, acylated at O1, is linked through a phospho group at O3 to O1 of D-myo-inositol
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Monoglycerides
description: A glyceride in which any one of the R groups (position not specified) is an acyl group while the remaining two R groups can be either H or alkyl groups
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: 2-Monolysocardiolipin
description: A phosphatidylglycerol consisting of cardiolipin lacking one fatty acyl group from the 2 or 2'-position
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: CDP-choline
description: A member of the class of phosphocholines that is the chloine ester of CDP. It is an intermediate obtained in the biosynthetic pathway of structural phospholipids in cell membranes
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Glycosphingolipids
description: A glycosphingolipid is a glycolipid that is a carbohydrate-containing derivative of a sphingoid or ceramide. It is understood that the carbohydrate residue is attached by a glycosidic linkage to O-1 of the sphingoid
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Plasmalogen
description: Any phospholipid that contains an olefinic function
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Lysophosphatidic acid
description: A member of the class of lysophosphatidic acids obtained by hydrolytic removal of one of the two acyl groups of any phosphatidic acid. A 'closed' class
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: FMN
description: A flavin mononucleotide that is riboflavin (vitamin B2) in which the primary hydroxy group has been converted to its dihydrogen phosphate ester
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: 1-phosphatidyl-1D-myo-inositol 4,5-bisphosphate
description: A phosphatidylinositol bisphosphate in which the two phosphate groups are at C-4 and C-5 of the inositol moiety which has the 1D-myo configuration
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Lysophosphatidylcholine
description: An acylglycerophosphocholine resulting from partial hydrolysis of a phosphatidylcholine, which removes one of the fatty acyl groups. The structure is depicted in the image where R1 = acyl, R2 = H or where R1 = H, R2 = acyl
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Glycerophospholipids
description: Any glycerolipid having a phosphate group ester-linked to a terminal carbon of the glycerol backbone
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: sn-glycerol 3-phosphate
description: An sn-glycerol 3-phosphate having unsubstituted hydroxy groups
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Ceramides
description: Ceramides (N-acyl-sphingoid bases) are a major subclass of sphingoid base derivatives with an amide-linked fatty acid. The fatty acids are typically saturated or monounsaturated with chain lengths from 14 to 26 carbon atoms; the presence of a hydroxyl group on carbon 2 is fairly common. Ceramides are generally precursors of more complex sphingolipids. In the illustrated generalised structure, R1 = OH, OX (where X = acyl, glycosyl, phosphate, phosphonate, etc.), or H
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: CDP-diacylglycerol
description: A CDP-glycerol having unspecified acyl groups (most commonly fatty acyl groups) at the 1- and 2-positions
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: L-Ascorbate
description: The L-enantiomer of ascorbate and conjugate base of L-ascorbic acid, arising from selective deprotonation of the 3-hydroxy group. Required for a range of essential metabolic reactions in all animals and plants
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: FAD
description: A flavin adenine dinucleotide in which the substituent at position 10 of the flavin nucleus is a 5'-adenosyldiphosphoribityl group
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Lysophosphatidylglycerol
description: A glycerophosphoglycerol resulting from partial hydrolysis of a phosphatidylglycerol, which removes one of the fatty acid groups. The structure is depicted in the image where R1 = acyl, R2 = H or where R1 = H, R2 = acyl
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Lysophosphatidylethanolamine
description: A glycerophosphoethanolamine resulting from partial hydrolysis of a phosphatidylethanolamine, which removes one of the fatty acid groups. The structure is depicted in the image where R1 = acyl, R2 = H or where R1 = H, R2 = acyl
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Coenzyme A
description: Coenzyme A is a coenzyme, notable for its role in the synthesis and oxidation of fatty acids, and the oxidation of pyruvate in the citric acid cycle
creator: Bruce May

name: Waxes
description: Waxes is a general term used to refer to the mixture of long-chain apolar lipids forming a protective coating (cutin in the cuticle) on plant leaves and fruits but also in animals (wax of honeybee, cuticular lipids of insects, spermaceti of the sperm whale, skin lipids, uropygial glands of birds, depot fat of planktonic crustacea), algae, fungi and bacteria. Some waxes are of mineral origin. Montan wax originates from mob or lignite, that fossilized compound representing a late step of the transformation of vegetal into hydrocarbons
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Sugars
description: Sugar is the generic name for sweet-tasting, soluble carbohydrates. They can be simple (monosaccharides such as glucose or fructose), double sugars (disaccharides such as sucrose or maltose) or long chains of sugars (polysaccharides such as starch or glycogen)
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Acetoacetyl-CoA
description: A 3-oxoacyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of acetoacetic acid
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: 5,6,7,8-tetrahydrobiopterin
description: Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4), also known as sapropterin, is a cofactor of the three aromatic amino acid hydroxylase enzymes, used in the degradation of amino acid phenylalanine and in the biosynthesis of the neurotransmitters serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5-HT), melatonin, dopamine, norepinephrine (noradrenaline), epinephrine (adrenaline), and is a cofactor for the production of nitric oxide (NO) by the nitric oxide synthases
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Phosphatidylcholine
description: A glycerophosphocholine that is glycero-3-phosphocholine bearing two acyl substituents at positions 1 and 2
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Collagen
description: The main structural protein in the extracellular matrix of the connective tissues of many animals.
creator: Steve Jupe

name: Phosphatidylethanolamine
description: A class of glycerophospholipids in which a phosphatidyl group is esterified to the hydroxy group of ethanolamine
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Riboflavin
description: D-Ribitol in which the hydroxy group at position 5 is substituted by a 7,8-dimethyl-2,4-dioxo-3,4-dihydrobenzo[g]pteridin-10(2H)-yl moiety. It is a nutritional factor found in milk, eggs, malted barley, liver, kidney, heart, and leafy vegetables, but the richest natural source is yeast. The free form occurs only in the retina of the eye, in whey, and in urine; its principal forms in tissues and cells are as flavin mononucleotide and flavin-adenine dinucleotide
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Lysobisphosphatidic acid
description: A lysophosphatidic acid having the unusual property of a phosphodiester moiety linked to positions sn-1 and sn1' of glycerol; and two additional fatty acids esterified to the glycerol head group
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Pantothenic acid
description: A member of the class of pantothenic acids that is an amide formed from pantoic acid and beta-alanine
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: 2-Monoglyceride
description: A monoglyceride in which the acyl substituent is located at position 2
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Cardiolipin
description: A phosphatidylglycerol composed of two molecules of phosphatidic acid covalently linked to a molecule of glycerol
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Thiamine
description: Thiamine, also known as thiamin or vitamin B1, is a vitamin found in food, and manufactured as a dietary supplement and medication. Food sources of thiamine include whole grains, legumes, and some meats and fish. Grain processing removes much of the thiamine content, so in many countries cereals and flours are enriched with thiamine. Supplements and medications are available to treat and prevent thiamine deficiency and disorders that result from it, including beriberi and Wernicke encephalopathy. Other uses include the treatment of maple syrup urine disease and Leigh syndrome
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Phosphoinositides
description: Any phosphatidylinositol that is phosphorylated at one or more of the hydroxy groups of inositol
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Fatty Alcohols
description: Fatty alcohols (or long-chain alcohols) are usually high-molecular-weight, straight-chain primary alcohols, but can also range from as few as 4–6 carbons to as many as 22–26, derived from natural fats and oils. The precise chain length varies with the source. Some commercially important fatty alcohols are lauryl, stearyl, and oleyl alcohols. They are colourless oily liquids (for smaller carbon numbers) or waxy solids, although impure samples may appear yellow. Fatty alcohols usually have an even number of carbon atoms and a single alcohol group (–OH) attached to the terminal carbon. Some are unsaturated and some are branched. They are widely used in industry. As with fatty acids, they are often referred to generically by the number of carbon atoms in the molecule, such as "a C12 alcohol", that is an alcohol having 12 carbons, for example dodecanol
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Phosphatidic acid
description: A derivative of glycerol in which one hydroxy group, commonly but not necessarily primary, is esterified with phosphoric acid and the other two are esterified with fatty acids
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: 1-phosphatidyl-1D-myo-inositol 3-phosphate
description: A phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate in which the inositol moiety is the D-myo-isomer
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: L-Dehydroascorbate
description: An organic anion and the conjugate base of L-dehydroascorbic acid, arising from deprotonation of the acidic C2-position
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Phosphatidyl-L-serine
description: A class of aminophospholipids in which a phosphatidyl group is esterified to the hydroxy group of serine
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: 1-phosphatidyl-1D-myo-inositols
description: A phosphatidylinositol in which the inositol moiety is the 1D-myo isomer and the phosphatidyl group is located at its position 1
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Cob(III)alamin
description: A cobalamin in which the central cobalt atom has an oxidation state of +3.
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Cobamamide
description: A member of the class of cobalamins that is vitamin B12 in which the cyano group is replaced by a 5'-deoxyadenos-5'-yl moiety. It is one of the two metabolically active form of vitamin B12
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Molybdopterin cofactor
description: A molybdopterin to which a metal or metal oxide is coordinated, and that acts as a prosthetic group
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate
description: The monophosphate ester obtained by condensation of phosphoric acid with the primary hydroxy group of pyridoxal
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Folic acid
description: An N-acyl-amino acid that is a form of the water-soluble vitamin B9. Its biologically active forms (tetrahydrofolate and others) are essential for nucleotide biosynthesis and homocysteine remethylation
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: (6S)-5,6,7,8-Tetrahydrofolic acid
description: A derivative of folic acid in which the pteridine ring is fully reduced; it is the parent compound of a variety of coenzymes that serve as carriers of one-carbon groups in metabolic reactions
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Pyridoxal
description: A pyridinecarbaldehyde that is pyridine-4-carbaldehyde bearing methyl, hydroxy and hydroxymethyl substituents at positions 2, 3 and 5 respectively. The 4-carboxyaldehyde form of vitamin B6, it is converted into pyridoxal phosphate, a coenzyme for the synthesis of amino acids, neurotransmitters, sphingolipids and aminolevulinic acid
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Nicotinic acid D-ribonucleotide
description: A D-ribonucleotide having nicotinic acid as the nucleobase
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Molybdate
description: A divalent inorganic anion obtained by removal of both protons from molybdic acid
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Dihydrofolic acid
description: A folic acid derivative acted upon by dihydrofolate reductase to produce tetrahydrofolic acid. It interacts with bacteria during cell division and is targeted by various drugs to prevent nucleic acid synthesis
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Pentose phosphate
description: Representation for a phospho sugar that is the phosphate derivative of pentose
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Biotin
description: An organic heterobicyclic compound that consists of 2-oxohexahydro-1H-thieno[3,4-d]imidazole having a valeric acid substituent attached to the tetrahydrothiophene ring. The parent of the class of biotins
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: N-ribosylnicotinamide
description: A pyridine nucleoside consisting of nicotinamide with a β-D-ribofuranosyl moiety at the 1-position
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Molybdopterin
description: A molybdopterin that is the O-phospho derivative of [(5aR,8R,9aR)-2-amino-4-oxo-6,7-disulfanyl-3,5,5a,8,9a,10-hexahydro-4H-pyrano[3,2-g]pteridin-8-yl]methanol
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: beta-Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate
description: An organophosphate oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of NADP+; major species at pH 7.3.
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: all-trans-decaprenyl diphosphate
description: A decaprenyl diphosphate having (E)-stereochemistry exclusively in the double bonds
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: ubiquinol-10
description: A ubiquinol in which the polyprenyl substituent is decaprenyl
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: AFB1
description: An aflatoxin having a tetrahydrocyclopenta[c]furo[3',2':4,5]furo[2,3-h]chromene skeleton with oxygen functionality at positions 1, 4 and 11
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Isopentenyl diphosphate
description: A prenol phosphate comprising 3-methylbut-3-en-1-ol having an O-diphosphate substituent
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Mercapturic acids
description: Mercapturic acid is a condensation product formed from the coupling of cysteine with aromatic compounds. It is formed as a conjugate in the liver and is excreted in the urine. Glutathione-S-transferase adducts lose glutamate and glycine portions, and are acetylated to form mercapturic acids, which are excreted
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Stereocilia
description: An actin-based protrusion from the apical surface of auditory and vestibular hair cells and of neuromast cells
creator: Bruce May

name: MET complex
description: Protein complex of the Mechanoelectrical transduction channel
creator: Bruce May

name: Cochlear nerve
description: A nerve in the head that carries signals from the cochlea of the inner ear to the brain
creator: Bruce May

name: Stem Cell
description: Relatively undifferentiated cells that retain the ability to divide and proliferate throughout postnatal life to provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized cells
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: Papillomavirus
description: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a viral infection that’s passed between people through skin-to-skin contact. There are over 100 varieties of HPV, more than 40 of which are passed through sexual contact and can affect your genitals, mouth, or throat
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: HCMV
description: A species of enveloped and spherical viruses with a capsid with T=16 icosahedral symmetry and surrounded by amorphous tegument, in the Herpesviridae family and Cytomegalovirus genus. The genome is composed of monopartite, linear double-stranded DNA. Human herpesvirus 5 is found in humans and causes mononucleosis-like symptoms in healthy individuals and pneumonia, hepatitis, encephalitis, myelitis, colitis, retinitis, neuropathy, mucoepidermoid carcinoma as well as other malignancies in immunocompromised persons, organ transplant recipients and newborn infants. Human herpesvirus 5 is transmitted congenitally or via direct person-to-person contact
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Tunnel of Corti
description: A triangular, fluid-filled space normally found between the inner and outer rows of supporting pillar cells in the organ of Corti
creator: Bruce May

name: PCDH15-CDH23
description: Graphic representation of two calcium-dependent cell-adhesion proteins, which are essential for maintenance of normal retinal and cochlear function
creator: Bruce May

name: Anti-inflammatory mediators
description: These are molecules of different nature that helps to the resolution of inflammation. These could be done at different points: suppressing the expression of pro-inflammatory genes, and the migration and activation of leukocytes, or promoting the inflammatory-cell clearance by apoptosis and phagocytosis. An example of anti-inflammatory mediator are the Lipoxins, which inhibit neutrophil migration and activation but promote the recruitment of monocytes and the phagocytic clearance of apoptotic cells by monocyte-derived macrophages
creator: Julieth Murillo

name: Lungs and Trachea
description: Graphic representation of lungs and trachea
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: HIV
description: Graphic representation of the Human Immunodeficiency Virus
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Influenza virus
description: Graphic representation of the Influenza virus
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Leishmania promastigote form
description: The promastigote form of Leishmania is found in the alimentary tract of sandflies. It is an extracellular and motile form. It is considerably larger and highly elongated, measuring 15-30 µm in length and 5 µm in width. It is spindle-shaped, tapering at both ends. A long flagellum (about the body length) is projected externally at the anterior end. The nucleus lies at the centre, and in front of it are the kinetoplast and the basal body
creator: Julieth Murillo

name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tb) is a species of pathogenic bacteria in the family Mycobacteriaceae and the causative agent of tuberculosis
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: CDH23
description: CDH23 is required for establishing and/or maintaining the proper organization of the stereocilia bundle of hair cells in the cochlea and the vestibule during late embryonic/early postnatal development
creator: Bruce May

name: Reticular lamina
description: A reticular lamina of epithelium that is part of a spiral organ of cochlea
creator: Bruce May

name: Listeria monocytogenes
description: Listeria monocytogenes is the species of pathogenic bacteria that causes the infection listeriosis. It is a facultative anaerobic bacterium, capable of surviving in the presence or absence of oxygen. It can grow and reproduce inside the host's cells and is one of the most virulent foodborne pathogens, with 20 to 30% of foodborne listeriosis infections in high-risk individuals may be fatal
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Lymph node
description: A lymph node or lymph gland is an ovoid or kidney-shaped organ of the lymphatic system and the adaptive immune system. Lymph nodes are widely present throughout the body and are linked by the lymphatic vessels
creator: Julieth Murillo

name: Enterobacteria
description: Enterobacteria are bacteria from the family Enterobacteriaceae, which are primarily known for their ability to cause intestinal upset. Enterobacteria are responsible for a variety of human illnesses, including urinary tract infections, wound infections, gastroenteritis, meningitis, septicemia, and pneumonia. Some are true intestinal pathogens; whereas others are merely opportunistic pests which attack weakened victims
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Inner hair cell
description: Inner hair cells (IHCs), the sensory cells of the cochlea, are responsible for signal transduction. Lying in a single row along the internal side of the tunnel of Corti
creator: Bruce May

name: SLC26A5 tetramer
description: Motor protein that converts auditory stimuli to length changes in outer hair cells and mediates sound amplification in the mammalian hearing organ. Prestin is a bidirectional voltage-to-force converter, it can operate at microsecond rates
creator: Bruce May

name: Leishmania amastigote form
description: The amastigote form of Leishmania is found in the mononuclear phagocytes and circulatory systems of humans. It is an intracellular and nonmotile form, being devoid of external flagella. The short flagellum is embedded at the anterior end without projecting out. It is oval in shape, and measures 3–6 µm in length and 1–3 µm in breadth. The kinetoplast and basal body lie towards the anterior end
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: Pro-Inflammatory mediators
description: These are molecules of different nature such as proteins, peptides, glycoproteins, cytokines, arachidonic acid metabolites (prostaglandins and leukotrienes), nitric oxide, and oxygen free radicals, among others, that are produced by epithelial cells, endothelial cells, or infiltrating inflammatory cells during inflammatory responses
creator: Julieth Murillo

name: Outer hair cell
description: The function of the outer hair cell in hearing is now perceived as that of a cochlear amplifier that refines the sensitivity and frequency selectivity of the mechanical vibrations of the cochlea
creator: Bruce May

name: Bacterial toxins
description: Graphic representation of bacteria related in diseases
creator: Bijay Jassal

creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: Leishmaniasis
description: Leishmaniasis is a disease caused by parasites of the Leishmania type. It is spread by the bite of certain types of sandflies. The disease can present in three main ways: cutaneous, mucocutaneous, or visceral
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: detailed TCR
description: A protein complex that contains a disulfide-linked heterodimer of T cell receptor (TCR) chains, which are members of the immunoglobulin superfamily, and mediates antigen recognition, ultimately resulting in T cell activation. The TCR heterodimer is associated with the CD3 complex, which consists of the nonpolymorphic polypeptides gamma, delta, epsilon, zeta, and, in some cases, eta (an RNA splice variant of zeta) or Fc epsilon chains
creator: Thawfeek Varusai

name: Trachea
description: The trachea is the portion of the airway that attaches to the bronchi as it branches

name: SARS-CoV-2
description: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is a strain of the species severe acute respiratory syndrome-related coronavirus (SARSr-CoV). It belongs to the family Coronaviridae which are a family of enveloped, positive-sense, single-stranded RNA viruses. SARS-CoV-2 likely originated from a bat coronavirus, to which is has a close genetic similarity. A highly contagious disease in humans, transmission occurs via liquid droplets from coughs or sneezes in a range of around 2 metres. SARS-CoV-2 is the cause of the ongoing pandemic of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)
creator: Bijay Jassal

creator: Bijay Jassal

TLRs (Toll-like receptors) control host immune response against pathogens through recognition of molecular patterns specific to microorganisms. TLR3 is a nucleotide-sensing TLR which is activated by double-stranded RNA, a sign of viral infection
creator: Thawfeek Varusai

creator: Thawfeek Varusai

name: JUN

creator: Thawfeek Varusai

name: L-methylmalonyl-CoA
description: A member of the class of malonyl-CoAs that is malonyl-CoA carrying a methyl group on the malony side chain
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: ATF2
description: Cyclic AMP-dependent transcription factor ATF-2 regulates the transcription of various genes, including those involved in anti-apoptosis, cell growth, and DNA damage response

name: C4b
description: C4b is derived from native C4 upon cleavage and release of C4a. It is prepared by cleavage of purified C4 with the classical pathway activated protease C1s enzyme
creator: Thawfeek Varusai

name: Carboxylases

name: CFD

name: Clostridium tetani
description: Clostridium tetani is a common soil bacterium and the causative agent of tetanus
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: PERTUZUMAB
description: Pertuzumab (also called 2C4) is a monoclonal antibody used in combination with trastuzumab and docetaxel for the treatment of metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer; it also used in the same combination as a neoadjuvant in early HER2-positive breast cancer
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: C3 convertase

creator: Thawfeek Varusai

name: tetX heavy chain

name: GNAT1

name: Ganglioside

name: C7
description: Constituent of the membrane attack complex (MAC) that plays a key role in the innate and adaptive immune response by forming pores in the plasma membrane of target cells. C7 serves as a membrane anchor

name: Bacillus anthracis

name: Cone cell BLUE
description: One of the two photoreceptor cell types in the vertebrate retina. In cones the photopigment is in invaginations of the cell membrane of the outer segment. Cones are less sensitive to light than rods, but they provide vision with higher spatial and temporal acuity, and the combination of signals from cones with different pigments allows color vision
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: ERBB2/EGFR heterodimer
description: Graphic representation of a heterodimer formed by Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-2 and Epidermal growth factor receptor

description: Corynebacterium diphtheriae[a] is the pathogenic bacterium that causes diphtheria
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: detailed MAC
description: The membrane attack complex (MAC) or terminal complement complex (TCC) is a structure typically formed on the surface of pathogen cell membranes as a result of the activation of the host's complement system, and as such is one of the effector proteins of the immune system. MAC forms transmembrane channels that disrupt the cell membrane of target cells, leading to cell lysis and death. Active MAC is composed of the subunits C5b, C6, C7, C8 and several C9 molecules
creator: Thawfeek Varusai

name: Clostridium botulinum
description: Clostridium botulinum is a Gram-positive, rod-shaped, anaerobic, spore-forming, motile bacterium with the ability to produce the neurotoxin botulinum
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: C9
description: Constituent of the membrane attack complex (MAC) that plays a key role in the innate and adaptive immune response by forming pores in the plasma membrane of target cells. C9 is the pore-forming subunit of the MAC

name: TRASTUZUMAB

creator: Thawfeek Varusai

name: Escherichia coli

name: botA heavy chain

name: C5 convertase
description: C5 convertase is an enzyme belonging to a family of serine proteases that play key role in the innate immunity. It participates in the complement system ending with cell death. There are four different C5 convertases able to specifically convert the protein C5 to C5a and C5b fragments. Two of the convertases are physiological complement enzymes, associate to the cell-surface and mediate the classical pathway (C4b2b3b, or C4b2a3b depending on source) or the alternative pathway (C3bBbC3b) of complement system

name: GYG

name: C4

Covalently binds to immunoglobulins and immune complexes and enhances the solubilization of immune aggregates and the clearance of IC through CR1 on erythrocytes. C4A isotype is responsible for effective binding to form amide bonds with immune aggregates or protein antigens, while C4B isotype catalyzes the transacylation of the thioester carbonyl group to form ester bonds with carbohydrate antigens

name: Transport vesicle membrane

name: Pathogenic alteration

name: C3
description: Complement C3 plays a central role in the activation of the complement system. Its processing by C3 convertase is the central reaction in both classical and alternative complement pathways. After activation C3b can bind covalently, via its reactive thioester, to cell surface carbohydrates or immune aggregates

name: Type II Alveolar Cell

name: Basophil

A second-generation HIV protease inhibitor, darunavir was designed to form robust interactions with the protease enzyme from many strains of HIV, including those from treatment-experienced patients with multiple resistance mutations to other protease inhibitors
creator: Marc Gillespie

name: SEMAXANIB
description: Semaxanib was a precursor in the development of the next generation kinase inhibitor ultimately approved as sunitinib.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: REGORAFENIB
description: Regorafenib is an inhibitor of multiple membrane-bound and intracellular kinases. Although the drug is approved it must carry a Boxed Warning alerting patients and clinicians that severe and fatal liver toxicity was observed in some patients in regorafenib clinical studies. Regorafenib is a Type-2 kinase inhibitor.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: SUNITINIB
description: Sunitinib is a Type-1 kinase inhibitor and was first approved by the US FDA and EMA in 2006.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: KW-2449
description: KW-2449 is a multi-targeted kinase inhibitor that was investigated as a treatment for leukemias with FLT3 mutations or T315I-mutated BCR/ABL translocation.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: MASITINIB
description: Using the trade name Masivet, this compound has been used for several years to treat mast cell tumours in dogs [6]. It is a receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) inhibitor, with inhibitory activity at the cKIT, platelet derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) and fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) RTKs.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: DHDDS
description: Dehydrodolichyl diphosphate synthase complex subunit DHDDS.
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: PONATINIB
description: Ponatinib is a Type-1 kinase inhibitor. It is a third generation BCR-Abl inhibitor. Use of ponatinib is subject to additional monitoring due to the observed serious risk of liver problems or blood clots (including heart attack and stroke, collectively referred to as arterial occlusive events, or AOEs).
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: QUIZARTINIB
description: Quizartinib (AC220) is a small molecule receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor, originally from Ambit Biosciences and later acquired by Daiichi Sankyo, that is currently under development for the treatment of acute myeloid leukaemia. Quizartinib is sold under the brand name Vanflyta in Japan. Its molecular target is FLT3, also known as CD135 which is a proto-oncogene.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: TAMATINIB
description: Tamatinib (R406) is a potent ATP-competitive (Type I) Syk inhibitor. It is the active form of the prodrug fostamatinib.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: GILTERITINIB
description: Gilteritinib is an orally bioavailable inhibitor of the receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) FMS-related tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3), AXL and anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK), with clinical antineoplastic activity. Gilteritinib inhibits the activity of FLT3-activating mutations which are one of the most common genetic alterations in acute myeloid leukemia (AML).
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: ALECTINIB
description: Alectinib is a second generation ALK inhibitor. It was developed to inhibit the expression of the mutated ALK gene that causes growth of some non-small cell lung cancers, in patients whose cancer has become resistant to the older ALK inhibitor, crizotinib. However, additional mutations may develop which confer alecitinib resistance. Cells harbouring these novel mutations are reported to be sensitive to ceritinib and other next-generation ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: LORLATINIB
description: Lorlatinib (PF-06463922) is a kinase inhibitor with action on ALK and ROS1 proto-oncogenes. It is a reversible, ATP-competitive small molecule inhibitor. Lorlatinib is a third generation ALK inhibitor designed to have improved blood-brain barrier penetrance compared to older second generation ALK inhibitors such as the approved drugs ceritinib, alectinib, and brigatinib, with the aim of better targeting metastatic NSCLC lesions in the brain. Advanced generation ALK inhibitors are those which target acquired ALK mutations resistant to the original first generation inhibitor crizotinib, which occur in virtually all AKL-rearranged NSCLC tumours within a year of starting crizotinib therapy. In fact, the cyano group of lortatinib is highly selective for the ALK mutation L1196M.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: IMATINIB
description:
Imatinib is a Type-2 kinase inhibitor. Its main inhibitory activity is against ABL kinase, but it has significant action at secondary targets including platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) and stem cell growth factor receptor (KIT).

Coronavirus: imatinib is reported to block Spike protein-induced SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV fusion in vitro, potentially by blocking Abl2 at the endosomal membrane and disrupting the actin dynamics that are required for virus-host fusion. It will be informative to determine if this holds true for SARS-CoV-2, and whether re-purposing of imatinib and/or newer Abl kinase inhibitors (dasatinib, bosutinib, ponatinib, nilotinib) could be a viable strategy against COVID-19. This approach would likely to be most effective during the early stage of infection.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: MIDOSTAURIN
description: Midostaurin is an analogue of staurosporine, and was originally described as a PKC inhibitor. It was later reported as an inhibitor of fms-related tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3).
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: PEXIDARTINIB
description: A pyrrolopyridine that is 5-chloro-1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine which is substituted by a [6-({[6-(trifluoromethyl)pyridin-3-yl]methyl}amino)pyridin-3-yl]methyl group at position 3. It is a potent multi-targeted receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor of CSF-1R, KIT, and FLT3 (IC50 of 20 nM, 10 nM and 160 nM, respectively). Approved by the FDA for the treatment of adult patients with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT).
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: GNG13
description: Guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(I)/G(S)/G(O) subunit gamma-13.
creator: Bruce May

name: HA(50)
description: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is s mucopolysaccharide composed of repeating N-acetylglucosamine and glucuronic acid subunits. HA(50) is a large HA fragment of around 20KDa formed when high molecular weight HA is cleaved during its degradation.
creator: Bijay Jassal

name: CRENOLANIB
description: Crenolanib (CP-868,596) is a potent and orally bioavailable benzamidazole Type I inhibitor of wild-type and mutant isoforms of the class III receptor tyrosine kinases FLT3 (FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3), PDGFRα (platelet-derived growth factor receptor), and PDGFRβ. It preferentially binds to phosphorylated active kinases in the 'DFG in' conformation.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: CRIZOTINIB
description: Critzotinib is a Type-1 kinase inhibitor and was first approved by the FDA in 2011. It inhibits ALK, cMET and ROS1 receptor tyrosine kinases. Critzotinib is a chiral molecule that exploits the three-dimensional space of the ATP pocket to achieve optimal potency and selectivity. The R-enantiomer as shown here exhibits better potency than the either the racemate or S-isomer and the approved drug should contain only the R-enantiomer.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: ASP-3026
description: ASP-3026 is a second generation ALK inhibitor designed to target ALK rearrangements which are the oncogenic drivers of some non-small cell lung cancers (NSCLCs) and T-cell lymphomas known as ALK- expressing anaplastic large-cell lymphoma (ALK+ALCL) .
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: NILOTINIB
description: Nilotinib is a Type-2 kinase inhibitor and was first approved by the FDA in 2007.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: LINIFANIB
description: Linifanib is a potent, orally active inhibitor of several receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), with principal targets being FLT3, CSF1R and VEGFR2.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: Gene deletion
description: A type of mutant phenotype evidence resulting from a mutation in which there is the removal of one or more contiguous nucleotides that may result in altered function or other measurable properties.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: CERITINIB
description: Ceritinib is a novel, highly selective, second generation ALK inhibitor.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: TANDUTINIB
description: Tandutinib is reported as a fms-related tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3) inhibitor, although it has almost identical IC50s for PDGRFβ and KIT.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: Bacteria with flagellum

name: LESTAURTINIB
description: Lestaurtinib was identified as an inhibitor of the receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) FLT3 (fms-related tyrosine kinase 3) with activity against leukemia cells in vitro and in vivo. It has activity against other RTKs. A drug repurposing sceen for breast cancer has identified lestaurtinib as a promising agent which appears to sensitise BRCA mutant and wild type breast cancer cells to the effects of the Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) inhibitor AG14361.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: MMAA

description: A collagen homotrimer of alpha1(III) chains; type III collagen triple helices associate to form fibrils.
creator: Bruce May

name: Mammary myoepithelial cell
description: A myoepithelial cell that is part of a mammary gland and is located in the basal layer. During lactation, a basal-myoepithelial cell of mammary gland contracts under the stimulation of oxytocin.
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: Lobule
description: Organ component of the mammary gland which consists of an aggregate of mammary alveoli that communicate with a lobular lactiferous duct.
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: Mammary alveolar cell
description: A milk-producing glandular epithelial cell that is part of a mammary gland alveolus.
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: ELN:FBN1 aggregate
description: Graphic representation of the association of elastin (ELN) and fibrillin-1 (FBN1) in the formation of elastic fibers.
creator: Bruce May

name: Degraded collagen fiber
description: Graphic representation of a collagen fibre after been degraded.
creator: Bruce May

name: Mammary stem cell
description: A multi-fate stem cell that is the source of cells for growth of the mammary gland during puberty and gestation. This cell type gives rise to both the luminal and myoepithelial cell types of the gland, and have been shown to have the ability to regenerate the entire organ in mice. This cell type also plays an important role in carcinogenesis of the breast.
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: Sweat gland
description: Any of the coil glands of the skin that secrete sweat.
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: PEP
description: An organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy and phosphate groups of phosphoenolpyruvic acid.
creator: Ralf Stephan

name: Chromosome Isometric 02
description: Isometric graphical representation of a chromosome.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: AFATINIB
description: Afatinib is a second-generation, irreversible, covalently-bound EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor. It potently and selectively inhibits EGFR and Erbb2. Although afatinib demonstrates improved activity against the gatekeeper EGFR T790M resistance mutation, it is equally potent against the wild-type receptor, leading to dose-limiting toxicities and a narrow safety window. Third generation, wild-type sparing inhibitors such as nazartinib are in development to circumvent this problem
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: LAPATINIB
description: Lapatinib is a Type-1.5 kinase inhibitor and was first approved by the US FDA in 2007.
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: Noradrenaline
description: An organic cation that is the conjugate acid of (R)-noradrenaline, obtained by protonation of the primary amino group.
creator: Ralf Stephan

name: Heterochromatin 01
description: A compact and highly condensed form of chromatin
creator: Kaiqiang You

name: NERATINIB
description: Neratinib is an irreversible inhibitor of the receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK), ErbB2. It also inhibits the related RTK, EGFR.
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: TESEVATINIB
description: Tesevatinib (XL-647) is an orally bioavailable small-molecule receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) inhibitor with broad spectrum activity againt EGFRs and VEGFRs [2], and which has pre-clinical antineoplastic potential.
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: DNA damaged base 02
description: Representation of a damaged DNA base
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: L-Citrulline
description: Zwitterionic form of L-citrulline having an anionic carboxy group and a protonated amino group.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: SUCCA
description: A dicarboxylic acid dianion resulting from the removal of a proton from both of the carboxy groups of succinic acid.
creator: Ralf Stephan

name: Dopaminium
description: An ammonium ion that is the conjugate acid of dopamine.
creator: Ralf Stephan

name: Manganese
description: A divalent metal cation in which the metal is manganese.
creator: Ralf Stephan

name: OSIMERTINIB
description: Osimertinib is a third-generation, potent, selective and irreversible inhibitor of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase bearing mutations which either sensitise the receptor, or cause drug resistance (eg the T790M mutation). The compound is less effective against the wild-type receptor.
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: AEE788
description: AEE788 is a reversible inhibitor of EGFR, HER2 and VEGFR1-3 with antitumor and antiangiogenic activity. This compound has been evaluated in phase I clinical trial where inhibition of EGFR was reported.
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: MAL
description: An optically active form of malate having (S)-configuration.
creator: Ralf Stephan

name: GABA
description: Zwitterionic form of γ-aminobutyric acid having an anionic carboxy group and a protonated amino group.
creator: Ralf Stephan

name: Urine
description: GRaphic representation of urine, a liquid containing excess water and water-soluble nitrogen-rich by-products of metabolism including urea, uric acid, and creatinine, which must be cleared from the bloodstream. Urinalysis detects these nitrogenous wastes in mammals.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: Carbamoyl phosphate
description: A doubly-charged organophosphate oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of carbamoyl phosphate; major species at pH 7.3.
creator: Karen Rothfels

name: SAPITINIB
description: Sapitinib is an inhibitor of all members of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) receptor tyrosine kinase family and was investigated as a potential oncology therapeutic.
creator: Marija Orlic-Milacic

name: T3/T4
description: Graphic representation of 3,3',5'-triiodo-L-thyronine zwitterion and L-thyroxine zwitterion.

name: Dipeptides

name: Generic transporter

name: CD8
description: T-cell surface glycoprotein CD8 alpha chain.

description: Graphic representation of nucleotide sugars which are the activated forms of monosaccharides. Nucleotide sugars act as glycosyl donors in glycosylation reactions. Those reactions are catalyzed by a group of enzymes called glycosyltransferases.

name: T cell progenitor
description: A lymphoid progenitor cell of the T cell lineage, with some lineage specific marker expression, but not yet fully committed to the T cell lineage.

name: L-Proline
description: The zwitterion formed from L-proline by proton transfer from the carboxy group to the ring nitrogen. It is the predominant species at physiological pH.

name: Tripeptides
description: Any oligopeptide that consists of three amino-acid residues connected by peptide linkages.

name: Naive CD4+ T cell
description: An antigen inexperienced CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell with the phenotype CCR7-positive, CD127-positive and CD62L-positive. This cell type develops in the thymus. This cell type is also described as being CD25-negative, CD62L-high, and CD44-low.
creator: Bruce May

name: Thymus gland
description: A single, unpaired primary lymphoid organ situated in the Mediastinum, extending superiorly into the neck to the lower edge of the Thyroid gland and inferiorly to the fourth costal cartilage. It is necessary for normal development of immunologic function early in life. By puberty, it begins to involute and much of the tissue is replaced by fat.
creator: Bruce May

name: Mitotic Metaphase
